discover.summary: This legacy system is a banking application that manages accounts, transfers, deposits, withdrawals, and settlements. It includes HTTP endpoints for creating and retrieving accounts, transferring funds, and running reconciliations. The system relies heavily on database triggers and functions for certain calculations and validations.

findings.summary: The `ledger_immutable` trigger prevents updates to immutable ledger entries.
The `calc_transfer_fee` function calculates transfer fees based on the transfer amount.
The `createTransfer` method uses a magic number for the fee threshold.

rules.title: Online transfer fee is zero below 100.00, otherwise 0.5% rounded HALF_UP with a 0.25 minimum
rules.description: The online fee path (Utils.calcXferFeeOnline, called by FeeCollector.collectFee for INTERNAL transfers) waives the fee entirely when the amount is strictly less than SMALL_XFER_LIMIT = 100.00, otherwise computes amount * 0.005 with setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP) and floors the result at MIN_FEE = 0.25. The database function calc_transfer_fee in V3 uses a different threshold (50) and a different rounding mode (ROUND, i.e. half-up on numeric) and a GREATEST floor of 0.25, so the two paths disagree for amounts in [50, 100).
rules.observableBehavior: POST /api/transfers with header Idempotency-Key (optional) and JSON body {"type":"INTERNAL","fromAccountId":<id>,"toAccountId":<id>,"amount":<n>} returns 201 with a body whose "fee" field is 0.00 when amount < 100.00, and otherwise equals max(round_half_up(amount*0.005, 2), 0.25) — e.g. amount 100.00 gives fee 0.50, amount 60.00 gives fee 0.25 on the online path but 0.30 via SELECT calc_transfer_fee(60). The fee is only non-zero when the source account's opened_at is less than 365 days before t…
assumptions: The source account exists and is ACTIVE; the transfer is INTERNAL so the online fee path is used.
The database NUMERIC(18,4) columns do not truncate the 2-decimal fee.

edgeCases.description: Amount exactly equal to the 100.00 waiver threshold.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The waiver does not apply (compareTo < 0 is false), so the fee is 0.50.

edgeCases.description: Source account opened 365 or more days before the transfer.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Fee is 0.00 and no FEE ledger row is written, even for a large amount.

edgeCases.description: Amount between 50 and 100 exclusive: the SQL function charges a fee while the online Java path waives it.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: SELECT calc_transfer_fee(60) returns 0.30 while the online transfer fee for 60.00 is 0.00.

rules.title: Batch-assessed transfer fee uses HALF_EVEN rounding and no 100.00 waiver
rules.description: SettlementBatch.run computes the fee for every PENDING transfer with Utils.calcXferFeeBatch, which applies amount * 0.005 with setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN) and a 0.25 floor but has no SMALL_XFER_LIMIT waiver, so a PENDING transfer of 60.00 is charged 0.30 by the batch while the online path charges 0.00. The batch also debits the fee before checking the principal balance, so a transfer that then fails the balance check keeps the fee and is marked FAILED with fee set.
rules.observableBehavior: POST /api/settlement/run returns 200 with JSON {"runId":<id>,"batchDate":"<yyyy-mm-dd>","processed":<n>,"failed":<n>,"requeued":<n>}. For a transfer left in status PENDING with amount 60.00, the run debits 0.30 from the source account and writes a ledger row with entry_type FEE and memo 'transfer fee (batch)'; GET /api/accounts/{id}/ledger shows that FEE row and the reduced balance. If the principal balance check then fails, the transfer row is set to status FAILED with fee 0.30 and the fee deb…
assumptions: At least one transfer row is in status PENDING when the batch runs.
The batch is not wrapped in a single transaction, so partial effects persist.

edgeCases.description: A PENDING transfer whose source account cannot cover the principal.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The fee is still debited, the transfer is marked FAILED with the fee recorded, and the run reports it in the failed count.

edgeCases.description: A FAILED transfer with retries already at 3 is not requeued by a later run.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The requeued count excludes it and its status stays FAILED.

rules.title: A ledger entry in status SETTLED cannot be updated or deleted unless the session sets app.correction_channel to CORRECTION_JOB
rules.description: The ledger_immutable trigger fires BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE on ledger_entries for each row and raises an exception when OLD.status = 'SETTLED' and the session setting app.correction_channel is anything other than 'CORRECTION_JOB'. CorrectionSvc.correct is the only writer that sets that channel, via SET LOCAL, and it is the only path that can move a settled entry to CORRECTED. The check is in the database, so it applies to every caller including direct SQL.
rules.observableBehavior: POST /api/corrections with JSON body {"transferId":<id>,"reason":"<text>","newAmount":<n or omitted>} returns 200 with {"transferId":<id>,"status":"REVERSED"|"SETTLED","reversedEntries":<n>,"newAmount":<n|null>,"newFee":<n>,"reason":"<text>"} and the previously SETTLED ledger rows for references XFER-<id> and FEE-<id> become status CORRECTED with matching REVERSAL rows inserted. The same UPDATE issued from any other session (no app.correction_channel set) fails with the E188 exception text 'E18…
assumptions: The trigger exists in the running database (V3 migration applied).
The correction request runs on a connection where SET LOCAL applies to the same transaction as the UPDATE.

edgeCases.description: Inserting a new ledger row that references a settled entry is not blocked by the trigger.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The INSERT succeeds; only UPDATE and DELETE on SETTLED rows raise E188.

edgeCases.description: Updating a ledger row whose status is POSTED rather than SETTLED.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The trigger does not raise, because the guard tests OLD.status = 'SETTLED'.

edgeCases.description: A correction requested for a transfer still in PENDING or PROCESSING.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: 400 BAD_REQUEST with the status echoed in the message; no ledger row is touched.

rules.title: A repeated POST /api/transfers with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original transfer with duplicate=true and 200 instead of 201
rules.description: createTransfer trims the Idempotency-Key header, looks the key up in transfers.idempotency_key (a UNIQUE column) and, on a hit, returns the stored transfer with dup=true and needsWire=false without touching balances or the ledger. The controller maps dup=true to HTTP 200 and dup=false to HTTP 201. The deposit path uses a different mechanism: it counts rows in request_log for channel 'DEPOSIT' and writes the key lower-cased, so a key differing only in case is a new deposit on the transfer path but a replay on the deposit path.
rules.observableBehavior: POST /api/transfers with header Idempotency-Key: K and body {"type":"INTERNAL","fromAccountId":<id>,"toAccountId":<id>,"amount":<n>} returns 201 with "duplicate":false on the first call; an identical second call with the same header returns 200 with "duplicate":true and the same "transferId", and the source and destination balances and the ledger row count are unchanged by the second call. POST /api/deposits with header Idempotency-Key: K and body {"accountId":<id>,"amount":<n>} returns 200 wit…
assumptions: The first request completed and committed before the replay is sent.
The client sends the same header value on the replay.

edgeCases.description: An Idempotency-Key header that is present but blank or whitespace.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The key is treated as absent, so the request is processed as a new transfer and no replay lookup happens.

edgeCases.description: The same key sent with different letter case on the transfer path.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The transfer path does not normalize case, so 'K' and 'k' are two distinct transfers; the deposit path lower-cases and would treat them as one.

rules.title: Transfers, deposits and withdrawals reject a missing, zero or negative amount with 400 BAD_REQUEST
rules.description: Every money-movement entry point parses the amount with Utils.amt and rejects it when it is null or its signum is not positive, throwing BadRequestException, which the controller's exception handler maps to HTTP 400 with error code BAD_REQUEST. The same guard is repeated in createTransfer, deposit and withdrawal, and the correction path applies the same positivity test to newAmount. A missing or unknown account is a separate rejection: NoSuchAccountException maps to 404 NO_SUCH_ACCOUNT.
rules.observableBehavior: POST /api/transfers with body {"type":"INTERNAL","fromAccountId":<id>,"toAccountId":<id>,"amount":0} returns 400 with body {"error":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"amount must be a positive number"}; the same holds for POST /api/deposits with {"accountId":<id>,"amount":-5} and POST /api/withdrawals with {"accountId":<id>,"amount":0}. Omitting "amount" entirely produces the same 400. A body naming an account id that does not exist returns 404 with {"error":"NO_SUCH_ACCOUNT"}. No ledger row and no balan…
assumptions: The request body is valid JSON and reaches the controller.

edgeCases.description: An amount supplied as a non-numeric string such as "abc".
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Utils.amt throws NumberFormatException, which is not a BadRequestException, so the generic handler returns 500 INTERNAL rather than 400.

edgeCases.description: An amount with more than four decimal places, e.g. 10.00005.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The value is accepted by the guard and stored in a NUMERIC(18,4) column, so the persisted amount may differ from the submitted amount.

invariants.statement: No ledger_entries row whose status is SETTLED can have its status or amount changed, or be deleted, by any session that has not set app.correction_channel to CORRECTION_JOB.
invariants.formalStatement: forall r in ledger_entries, forall session s: (r.status = 'SETTLED' and s.app.correction_channel <> 'CORRECTION_JOB') implies (UPDATE r or DELETE r raises exception 'E188')
knownExceptions: Sessions that set app.correction_channel = 'CORRECTION_JOB' are exempt by design; CorrectionSvc.correct is the only such writer found in the repository.
INSERT into ledger_entries is not guarded by the trigger, so new rows referencing settled entries are permitted.
invariants.checkingStrategy: In a session that has not set app.correction_channel, attempt UPDATE ledger_entries SET status = 'CORRECTED' WHERE id = <id of a SETTLED row> and then DELETE FROM ledger_entries WHERE id = <same id>; both statements must raise the E188 exception and leave the row unchanged. Then repeat the UPDATE in a session that first runs SET LOCAL app.correction_channel = 'CORRECTION_JOB' and confirm it succeeds. Finally, verify that no row with status SETTLED has a changed amount by comparing a snapshot of (id, amount, status) taken before and after each scenario.

invariants.statement: At most one transfers row exists for any non-null idempotency_key, and a replay of a request carrying an already-used key creates no additional ledger entry and no balance change.
invariants.formalStatement: forall k: count(select 1 from transfers where idempotency_key = k) <= 1 and (replay with key k) implies (ledger_entries row count and accounts.balance unchanged)
knownExceptions: The deposit path does not use transfers.idempotency_key; it journals into request_log with the key lower-cased, so case variants of the same key are not deduplicated there.
invariants.checkingStrategy: For a fixed key K: record the source and destination balances and the ledger row count for the account, POST /api/transfers with Idempotency-Key: K, record the same three values, POST the identical request again with the same header, and assert that the second response has duplicate=true, the same transferId, and that balances and ledger row count are identical to the post-first-call snapshot. Then run the uniqueness query to confirm no key appears twice. Repeat with two concurrent requests carrying K and record whether the second fails on the UNIQUE constraint.

unknowns.question: Which fee path a given channel actually reaches at runtime: the online Utils.calcXferFeeOnline path, the batch Utils.calcXferFeeBatch path, or the SQL calc_transfer_fee function?
Does GET /api/accounts/{id} return a stale balance after a transfer, deposit or withdrawal, because AcctSvc.getAcct serves the value from BAL_CACHE when present?
Can the reconciliation report ever record a non-zero discrepancies count, given that ReconSvc.run always inserts the literal 0 and the status 'IN_BALANCE' while separately counting adjustments?
What does a caller observe when the audit write fails after the correction's ledger writes have already succeeded?

When the wire adapter times out for an EXTERNAL transfer, does the transfer remain PENDING and settle on the next POST /api/settlement/run, and does the retry with the same Idempotency-Key return the PENDING receipt rather than resubmitting?
